Maya T: Quick RFC follow-up — I posted the modularization playbook draft in docs. TL;DR: phased approach to split large runtime modules into smaller deployable units over ~12 months. Main questions: ownership model, migration order, and how we buy down debt without stalling feature work.

Arjun Patel: skimmed it. +1 to phase gating. prefer interface-first (thin facade) before any state split. keep shared DB read-only for phase 1. :+1:

Samir Chen: agree on facade-first. also: we need an explicit canary + rollback plan per phase. propose a standard checklist (metrics, smoke tests, fallback route).

Olivia Park: big concern is tenant routing and tail latency — if we split hotpath services we must measure per-tenant p95 before/after. can we add perf baselines to the playbook? :thinking_face:

Maya T: yes — I'll add a perf baseline section. proposal: each split must include a perf test harness, a cost delta estimate, and a migration rollback ticket. also recommend a temporary dual-write only when we have safe cutover scripts.

Arjun Patel: +1 on dual-write but keep it limited. we should avoid long-lived dual-writes (data drift, complexity). instead: short overlap window + automated reconciliation. add a schema-migration checklist (backfill, forward-compat, idempotent ops).

Samir Chen: for tech-debt paydown, suggest reserving a 20% sprint lane for refactor work tied to each service cutover. otherwise product teams deprioritize. we can allow feature toggles to gate risk.

Olivia Park: who owns the rollout guardrails? infra or owning product team? we need a single decision arbiter for rollback during a cutover window.

Maya T: propose the owning team leads the cutover with eng-platform as runway/ops support. eng-platform owns the rollback tooling and canary dashboards. the owning team owns migration correctness + test coverage.

Arjun Patel: sounds good. one more tradeoff: packaging vs service split. packaging is cheaper short-term (fewer infra costs) but prolongs coupling. service split is costlier early but pays off on velocity and isolation. we should explicitly call this tradeoff in the playbook and provide decision criteria.

infra-bot: Deploy-bot: FYI — rough infra cost projection for a medium split: +18% GPU/instance baseline during cutover, +6% steady-state. link: https://internal.redwood/costs/simulations (internal)

Maya T: thanks infra-bot. action items: (1) I'll update the playbook with perf baseline, rollout checklist, and schema checklist by EOW. (2) Arjun — can you draft the decision criteria table for packaging vs split? (3) Samir — please prototype a standard canary dashboard template we can reuse. (4) Olivia — add tenant-specific perf gating thresholds.

Arjun Patel: on it.

Samir Chen: will spin up a dashboard proto tomorrow.

Olivia Park: adding gating thresholds to board now.

Maya T: great — let's try to land an initial pilot (one non-hot enrichment path) in the next 8 weeks. low-risk, measurable. will share updated doc in #architecture when done. :rocket:
